name: Asgard
description: The realm of the Æsir gods, located at the top of Yggdrasil. Asgard is a majestic realm of golden halls and celestial beauty, home to Odin's hall Valhalla and connected to Midgard by the rainbow bridge Bifröst. It is the seat of divine power and the gathering place of the gods.

characteristics.environment: Ethereal golden realm with magnificent halls and celestial architecture
characteristics.culture: Warrior culture focused on honor, wisdom, and preparation for Ragnarök
characteristics.significance: The seat of divine power and home to the ruling gods of Norse mythology

name: Vanaheim
description: The realm of the Vanir gods, masters of magic, fertility, and prosperity. Vanaheim is a lush, verdant world of natural beauty and abundant resources. The Vanir are associated with nature, fertility, wisdom, and the ability to see the future. After the Æsir-Vanir War, the two pantheons exchanged hostages to ensure peace.

characteristics.environment: Lush forests, fertile fields, and abundant natural resources
characteristics.culture: Focused on magic, fertility, prosperity, and harmony with nature
characteristics.significance: Home of the Vanir, the second pantheon of Norse gods

name: Alfheim
description: The realm of the Light Elves, beings of ethereal beauty and magical prowess. Alfheim is a luminous world of perpetual twilight, filled with enchanted forests and crystalline structures. The Light Elves are closely associated with the Vanir and are considered benevolent beings who bring beauty and light to the cosmos.

characteristics.environment: Luminous realm of perpetual twilight with enchanted forests
characteristics.culture: Focused on beauty, magic, artistry, and harmony
characteristics.significance: Home of the Light Elves, beings of light and magic

name: Midgard
description: The realm of humans, positioned in the middle of the cosmic tree. Midgard is encircled by a vast ocean where the Midgard Serpent Jörmungandr dwells. It is connected to Asgard by the rainbow bridge Bifröst and is the home of mortal men and women. The gods take great interest in Midgard and often interact with humanity.

characteristics.environment: Mortal world of varied landscapes encircled by ocean
characteristics.culture: Diverse human societies with varying customs and beliefs
characteristics.significance: The realm of humanity and center of the cosmic order

name: Jotunheim
description: The realm of the giants (Jötnar), beings of immense size and power who often oppose the gods. Jotunheim is a harsh, mountainous world of extreme conditions and untamed wilderness. The giants represent the chaotic forces of nature and are both enemies and occasional allies of the gods. Many gods have giant ancestry.

characteristics.environment: Harsh mountains, frozen wastes, and untamed wilderness
characteristics.culture: Strong, chaotic, representing the wild forces of nature
characteristics.significance: Home of the giants, the ancient enemies and occasional allies of the gods

name: Svartalfheim
description: The realm of the Dwarves (also called Dark Elves), master craftsmen and smiths. Svartalfheim is a subterranean world of vast caverns, underground forges, and mineral wealth. The dwarves created many of the gods' most powerful artifacts, including Thor's hammer Mjölnir, Odin's spear Gungnir, and Freyr's ship Skíðblaðnir.

characteristics.environment: Underground caverns, forges, and mines filled with precious metals
characteristics.culture: Master craftsmen and smiths, creators of legendary artifacts
characteristics.significance: Source of the gods' most powerful weapons and magical items

name: Muspelheim
description: The realm of fire, ruled by the fire giant Surtr. Muspelheim is a scorching world of eternal flames, molten rock, and unbearable heat. It existed before the creation of the cosmos and will play a crucial role in its destruction during Ragnarök, when Surtr leads his legions to burn the Nine Realms. It is the opposite of icy Niflheim.

characteristics.environment: Realm of eternal fire, molten rock, and scorching heat
characteristics.significance: Primordial realm of fire that will consume the world at Ragnarök

name: Niflheim
description: The primordial realm of ice, mist, and darkness. Niflheim is a frozen wasteland of eternal winter, existing since before the creation of the cosmos. Within Niflheim lies the well Hvergelmir, the source of many rivers, and it is closely associated with Helheim. The meeting of fire from Muspelheim and ice from Niflheim in the void of Ginnungagap sparked the creation of the cosmos.

characteristics.environment: Frozen wasteland of ice, mist, and eternal darkness
characteristics.culture: Primordial and lifeless, the opposite of Muspelheim
characteristics.significance: Primordial realm of ice and one of the first realms to exist

name: Helheim
description: The realm of the dishonored dead, ruled by the goddess Hel. Helheim is a cold, misty realm where those who died of disease, old age, or without honor reside. It is distinct from Valhalla, where warriors who died in battle go. Helheim is described as a gloomy place, though not necessarily a place of punishment. Hel herself is half-living and half-dead in appearance.

characteristics.environment: Cold, misty realm of the dead with gloomy halls
characteristics.culture: Silent realm of those who died without honor in battle
characteristics.significance: The underworld where most mortals go after death
